packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-07 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reading)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading for this
fragment. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..010 in packet-07 (and listed the directory).
I did not open packet.json and used no search. I have not tried to identify the work.
The only external text seen is the modern pencil shelfmark on the leaf itself
("Stams, STA, Frg. 162r" / "162v").

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two overviews: image-001 (face labelled in pencil "Frg. 162r") and image-006 ("Frg. 162v").
  Tiles: image-002..005 belong to 162r; image-007..010 to 162v.
- Support looks like paper (chain/laid lines visible in tiles), a single trimmed piece with a
  vertical fold/crease near the left third. Upright orientation.
- Two columns per face, written in brown ink, a late-medieval German (Upper German) cursive.
  On 162r the left column is cut away on its left side (line beginnings lost); the right column
  is nearly complete but loses a few letters at the right edge. On 162v the reverse: left column
  nearly complete (first letters lost at left edge), right column cut on its right side.
- No coloured initials. Key terms (names, Latin terms) are enclosed in ink boxes or underlined
  with long ink strokes (e.g. "Zentrio", "Zenturio", "sacrament", "throni", "potestates",
  "angeli", "Ierarchia", "tobia", "dionisi"). Paragraph mark (pilcrow-like stroke) before
  "der sechst chor". Some faint red traces at right edge of 162r col b (no legible rubric).
- Tentative interpretation only: vernacular prose, apparently instructional/sermon-like,
  with cited authorities (david, gregorius, dionysius) and a sequence of numbered angelic
  "chor" (choirs). 162r col a treats a centurion and a sacrament.

SPANS SELECTED: 162r col b (whole, the choir sequence 3rd-6th), 162r col a (all visible line
ends), 162v col a (whole, choirs 7th-9th + "Ierarchia"), 162v col b (visible line beginnings).
Nothing left unread except the cut-away portions. Wider view is not possible: text is lost
physically at the trimmed edges.

Conventions: (expansion), word? = uncertain, [illegible], [..] = text lost at cut edge.
"dz" = dz with abbreviation (das/daz). Line numbers count visible text lines from top of the
named tile. Long s rendered as s.
